questions.q: What is the shape of a Salesforce REST API error response body?
options: A JSON array of error objects, even when there's only one error
A single JSON object with a message field
A plain text string
An XML document, regardless of the Accept header
questions.explain: Salesforce always returns errors as a JSON array of objects (each with message, errorCode, and sometimes fields), even for just one error — code must parse it as an array.

questions.q: A request fails with HTTP 401 and errorCode INVALID_SESSION_ID. What does this mean, and what should you do?
options: The record doesn't exist — delete the request
The access token is missing or expired — obtain a new token and retry the call once
The org has run out of storage space
The request body was malformed JSON
questions.explain: 401/INVALID_SESSION_ID means the token itself is the problem — refreshing or re-obtaining the token and retrying once is the correct response, not retrying the identical failed call.

questions.q: A request fails with HTTP 400 and errorCode REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING. Should you retry the exact same request?
options: Yes, immediately and repeatedly until it succeeds
Yes, but only after waiting 24 hours
Only if the object is a custom object
No — the request itself is wrong and will fail identically every time until the missing field is added to the payload
questions.explain: A 400 with REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING is a client-side request problem, not a transient failure — retrying the same payload will fail the same way every time.

questions.q: Which HTTP status code, paired with errorCode REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, indicates an org has hit its API allocation?
options: 200 OK
201 Created
403 Forbidden
500 Internal Server Error
questions.explain: REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED pairs with a 403 Forbidden response, distinct from permission-based 403s, when an org's API request allocation is exhausted.

questions.q: What is the recommended strategy for handling a transient 500 Internal Server Error or a 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED response?
options: Retry immediately in a tight loop with no delay
Never retry under any circumstances
Retry with backoff — waiting progressively longer between attempts rather than hammering the API immediately
Delete the record and recreate it
questions.explain: Transient failures like a 500 or a temporary rate limit are the right candidates for retry-with-backoff, as opposed to request-validity errors like a missing required field.
